body:
Seems to be related to:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105642

Though this looks related to initial construction.

> The collision shape positions are updated on every frame as the rope moves.

Forgive me for not actually looking at your library, but what is the purpose of this moving of individual shapes? Are the rope segments just individual collision shapes, and this is the simulation state sync?

If so, I feel like that maybe shouldn't be the case, ideally, since shapes have no velocities themselves, so any collision response imparted by moving them (if that's even a thing in your case) would purely be as a result of Jolt's error correction, which will likely look quite "dulled". Having these be individual bodies (with `BODY_MODE_RIGID` or `BODY_MODE_KINEMATIC`) would likely be the preferred approach, similar to how you would typically set up a ragdoll with each body part being individual bodies rather than individual shapes.

Would that work in your case, or have I misunderstood the purpose of these shape transformations?

> but what is the purpose of this moving of individual shapes?

"Why is your rigid body not rigid?" is a fair question :)

One use case is Area3D can detect the rope entering or exiting. It also allows cheap (at least in GodotPhysics) objects to react to the rope (but not for the rope to react to objects).

>  Having these be individual bodies (with BODY_MODE_RIGID or BODY_MODE_KINEMATIC) would likely be the preferred approach, similar to how you would typically set up a ragdoll with each body part being individual bodies rather than individual shapes.

Possibly. However, the perf for updating a collision shape within a rigid body has other use cases beside responding physics collisions.  At the very least, Joly should probably be deferring the rebuild until the end of the next frame, instead of on every shape transform update?

As written, it looks like it has what looks like O(N^2) perf for setting the shape transform.

> Would that work in your case, or have I misunderstood the purpose of these shape transformations?

Honestly, I haven't tried it that. Currently, I'm using the ray caster for collision detection as 300+ capsules on screen is more expensive than 300 ray collisions.

I might try this though, just to see how it performs.

> At the very least, Jolt should probably be deferring the rebuild until the end of the next frame, instead of on every shape transform update?

Yes, I didn't mean to imply that this issue is a non-issue. As talked about in #105642 we've [discussed](https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/discussions/1165) ways to address this, but the way I would ideally want to do it involves a big and scary refactoring that I've been putting off. In most cases there has usually been a simple workaround as well, like performing the shape changes out-of-tree, which avoids much of this overhead you're seeing.

In this case though, it does sound like having it be individual bodies rather than shapes is the more correct approach either way, assuming I haven't misunderstood some part of it.

> scary refactor

Relatable :)

I tried your suggested approach (body-per-link), and I think the performance of building individual bodies isn't going to work for my use case. One of the problems concerns the exclusion list and self intersection.

At the moment I'm going to contend myself to just not have my rope objects do one-sided collisions. They can respond against other objects when moving but won't move when acted upon by another external object.

Like so: https://bsky.app/profile/esteeland.bsky.social

This is not the forum for a conversation on the topic, but I would love to discuss a strategy for implementing bi-directional collisions with rope/chain using other strategies. I will see if I can find you on the dev forum.

I will leave this issue open as the underlying problem it exposes still exists.

> One of the problems concerns the exclusion list and self intersection.

I assume you're aware of the `body_add_collision_exception`/`body_remove_collision_exception` methods in `PhysicsServer3D`? Maybe that's what you mean by exclusion list?

> This is not the forum for a conversation on the topic, but I would love to discuss a strategy for implementing bi-directional collisions with rope/chain using other strategies. I will see if I can find you on the dev forum.

I doubt I can be of much help there. I still don't consider myself much of a physics programmer, as my knowledge beyond the library integration part is pretty shallow.

> I will leave this issue open as the underlying problem it exposes still exists.

Since this is essentially just a duplicate of #105642 I'll go ahead and close this as such. I rephrased the title of #105642 to maybe better encompass this.
